newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian shares up in dull post-Christmas trade.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian shares up in dull post-Christmas trade.

text.p: Oil shares moved the Nigerian stock market higher on Friday, the first day of business after the Christmas break, traders said.
The all-share index was yet to be updated because of technical problems.
The number of traders dwindled from the pre-Christmas level of more than 60 to 17 on Friday with a sharp drop in turnover.
Oil marketing companies, the toast of the market, were the main gainers amidst scanty deals.
Unipetrol gained 30 kobo to close at 58.55 naira while African Petroleum was 44.85 naira, up 20 kobo.
Conglomerate UAC was a surprise 10 kobo gainer at 7.40 naira, the same as Union Bank which ended at 5.80 naira in speculative dealing.
Construction firm Roads Nigeria Ltd gained 10 kobo to 50 kobo after returning to profitability.
West African Portland Cement Company went five kobo up to 46.20 naira, the same as Delta Glass which closed at 6.90 naira following renewed demand.
Losers included Ashaka Cement which slid to 16.70 naira, down 10 kobo, stationery firm Thomas Wyatt, down two kobo at 6.38 naira and African Paints, one kobo lower at 1.68 naira.
